title.narrative: Activity under preparation PRISM: EU-Ghana Partnership for a Regular, Inclusive, Sustainable and nationally owned Migration governance system

description.narrative: The Action is embedded in a broader continuum of EU interventions on migration governance, return and reintegration, and legal pathways which has positioned the European Union as a leading donor and trusted partner of Ghana on migration. It complements this series of EU initiatives by supporting the progressive consolidation of national ownership in migration governance and by facilitating the transition from initial groundwork on legal pathways towards a more coordinated, systemic and higher-impact approach to labour migration. In particular, the Action reinforces the Individual Measure by embedding reintegration efforts within a broader framework of improved migration governance, and by extending both the timeframe and the financial resources to deliver quality services to returnees through national actors.The PRISM Action introduces several important innovations compared to previous interventions: i) it operationalises the Team Europe approach by bringing together four EU Member States¿ development agencies (Germany, Italy, France and Spain) in joint implementation; ii) for the first time in Ghana, labour migration will be addressed in a structured and coherent manner; iii) a more prominent role for civil society in migration governance, alongside a specific focus on decentralised levels will maximise impact and ensure sustainability.The overall objective is to strengthen Ghanaian capacities to manage a nationally owned and sustainable migration governance system, including implementing human rights-based reintegration policies and mutually beneficial labour migration schemes with EU Member States, including Germany, Italy and France. Building on a comprehensive approach to migration, the Action recognises that, alongside reintegration dynamics, Ghana¿s priorities also relate to other key aspects of mobility, including the protection of vulnerable migrants such as Internally Displaced Persons and refugees from Burkina Faso. This comprehensive approach is reflected in the title, as the PRISM acronym underlines the multiple dimensions of the migration phenomenon. In this perspective, the proposed action intends to contribute to MIP Priority Area 3 (Good governance and security), and more specifically to Result 1.4 (A coherent and comprehensive management of migration in all its aspects is reinforced). It is also aligned with the MIP Mid-Term Review, which calls for an integrated approach to migration, encompassing migration governance, reintegration and support to legal mobility.The Action is structured around two main components. The first component focuses on migration governance and builds on the significant progress achieved by Ghana in recent years at policy and coordination level, such as the establishment of the first whole-of-government National Coordination Mechanism on migration and the development of the National Referral Mechanism for returnees and vulnerable migrants. Further enhancement of the Ghanaian migration governance system will be pursued through four lines of intervention: (i) enhancing governmental capacities to operationalise the unified National Referral Mechanism for vulnerable migrants, including returnees; (ii) strengthening national coordination mechanisms for the implementation of migration policy priorities; (iii) mainstreaming migration into local development planning; and (iv) enhancing civil society participation within a whole-of-society, community-based and human rights¿based approach.The second component further develops and promotes legal pathways within a framework rooted in human rights, gender¿responsive governance and a full Team Europe spirit.
